field_notes.hospitalized: Collected only in the current file (from 2025-06-16): the archive severity labels do not say whether an injury was hospital-treated, so it is never true before the change.
field_notes.hour: Local hour of the incident time, null when not given. Tesla, Inc. files times in UTC; they are converted to the local time of the report's state (time_basis = utc). See time_rule.
field_notes.light_from_time: Approximate, derived from incident time and month (see light_rule).
field_notes.lighting: Collected only in the archive file (through 2025-06-15); use light_from_time to compare across the change.

light_check.note: rows: recorded Lighting (daylight = day, dawn/dusk = twilight, any dark = night); columns: derived from time. 'opposite' counts day read as night or night read as day; day_night_agreement = 1 - opposite / reports where neither side is twilight.
light_check.unit: archive-era reports with both a recorded Lighting value and an incident time

light_rule: Approximate light condition from the incident clock time and month: one US-wide table of sunrise and sunset (latitude 37 N, the 15th of the month, solar noon 20 minutes after the time-zone meridian, daylight saving time March to October except Arizona and Hawaii) with a +-60 minute twilight band around sunrise and sunset. Night = more than 60 minutes after sunset or before sunrise. Approximate: actual light depends on the exact place and date, which the public data does not give.

not_engaged.note: Reports whose Engagement Status is 'Verified Not Engaged' (a field of the current file, from 2025-06-16) are not counted as crashes of the program: the filer verified that the automation was off. They stay in the golden database and in revisions.json. 'Alleged Engaged' reports are counted, as filed.

offline_note: Raw files were not downloaded in this run: the sha256 values in fetch_log come from the previous fetch log and were not re-verified, and row-drop checks compare against the previous fetch log only.

robust_definition.ads: Any injury or fatality, or an air bag deployed (any vehicle), or any vehicle towed, or a pedestrian, cyclist, scooter/skateboard or other non-motorist crash partner (structured fields).
robust_definition.l2: Any injury or fatality, or an air bag deployed, or a pedestrian, cyclist, scooter/skateboard or other non-motorist crash partner. A tow-away alone does not count for Level 2.
robust_definition.name: Injury, air bag, tow-away (ADS) or VRU: comparable across the 2025-06-16 rule change
uncertainty: Inferred from the data pattern (Waymo: no-injury, no-airbag, not-towed crashes per mile fell to a third at the change while the rest stayed flat; Tesla: tow-only reports fell from about 20% to 1-4%), not from a re-reading of the order's text.

A criterion whose field is unknown counts as not met, so the class is a lower bound. Air bag is unknown in about 15% of archive-era reports (mostly Level 2); towed is unknown in about 92% of current-era Level 2 reports (towed is not used for Level 2) and in a few percent of ADS reports.
Any injury includes injuries without hospital treatment. The archive severity labels do not say whether an injury was hospital-treated.
Tesla Level 2 severity is unknown in about 94% of reports, so its robust class is close to 'air bag deployed'.
robust_definition.why: Under the Third Amended SGO (effective 2025-06-16) minor ADS crashes without injury, air bag or tow-away largely stopped being reported, and tow-away-only Level 2 reports nearly vanished. Crashes meeting these criteria were reportable before and after the change, so their counts can be compared across it.

tag_rules.description: Narrative mentions any of: "red light", "red lights", "traffic light", "traffic lights", "traffic signal", "traffic signals", "stop light", "stop lights", "stoplight", "stoplights", "stop sign", "stop signs", "signalized", "ran a light", "ran the light", "run a light", "run the light". Plain "signal" is not matched, so a turn signal does not count.
Lighting is dark and unlit, dark with unknown lighting, or dawn/dusk. Dark with street lighting (dark_lighted) does not count, because lit roads are not reduced visibility in the way unlit ones are.
Weather includes fog, rain, snow or dust storm.
Narrative mentions any of: "glare", "sun glare", "sunlight", "sun in", "setting sun", "rising sun", "low sun", "the sun", "direct sun", "blinded", "blinding", "low visibility", "poor visibility".
Subject vehicle movement is Lane / Road Departure.
Crash was with a fixed object or pole/tree and the subject vehicle speed was at least 25 mph. Unknown speed does not qualify.
Subject vehicle was moving (movement is anything except stopped, parked, unknown, other or blank) and the crash partner was stopped or parked.
Crash was with a fixed object, pole/tree or first-responder vehicle.
Narrative mentions any of: "debris", "stalled", "emergency vehicle", "emergency vehicles", "cone", "cones".
Subject vehicle speed was at most 5 mph (0 counts; unknown does not).
Subject vehicle movement was stopped or parked (it was struck).
Crash was with a pedestrian, cyclist, scooter/skateboard or other non-motorist.
Crash partner movement is a non-motorist movement (nm_*).

time_rule: Incident times are used as filed (local time), except Tesla, Inc. reports, which are filed in UTC: those are converted to the local time of the report's state (most populous time zone; daylight saving time March to October by incident month). Evidence: in the archive file Tesla's recorded Lighting agrees with the time-derived light in 55% of day/night reports as filed and 96% after converting; every other reporter agrees best as filed.
